item.title: Balerdi nears permanent deal to Roma for €11-14 million
item.description: Balerdi nears permanent deal to Roma for €11-14 million In just a few weeks, Leonardo Balerdi has carved out an increasingly important role for Gian Piero Gasperini’s Roma. The Argentine defender has already logged 468 minutes of action, scoring a brace in the away match at the Maradona. These performances have brought the player closer to triggering the buy option held by the Giallorossi. As reported by Il Messaggero , Balerdi’s option is tied to specific contractual conditions that will also determine his fee. If the defender were to play 55% of the season’s matches, playing a minimum of 45 minutes in each game, the option would start at €14 million. The figure would be €3 million lower, dropping to €11 million, if the Argentine were to play between 40% and 55% of matches, failing to reach the latter threshold. The minutes he’s accumulated so far and the space he’s found in Gasperini’s rotations therefore bring Balerdi closer to reaching the terms of the agreement. The defender has quickly earned the coach’s trust, becoming an increasingly frequent presence in the Giallorossi squad.

item.title: City's Maresca expects no let-up from Brighton in second straight game
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca reacts ahead of the English Premier League soccer match between Manchester City and Sunderland at the Etihad Stadium. (is associated with: «City's Maresca expects no let-up from Brighton in second straight game») Martin Rickett/PA Wire/dpa Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca expects another tough test from Brighton at the weekend as the sides meet again after a compelling cup tie. Holders City edged past the Seagulls on penalties to reach the League Cup quarter-finals on Wednesday after twice coming from behind to draw 2-2 at the Etihad Stadium. After making 16 changes between them, both Maresca and opposite number Fabian Hürzeler are likely to restore full-strength teams when they renew their rivalry at the same venue on Saturday in the Premier League. But Maresca has “no doubt” the visitors will prove just as tough to beat. The Italian said: “They are in a brilliant moment. They are winning games, they are scoring goals. They are scoring many goals every game – three, four, five, goals a game. “I’ve watched all their Premier League games since we started, and since the first day – against Arsenal, (Crystal) Palace, Liverpool, they always go front foot, man to man. “We knew that this was a tough game and they’re going to be exactly the same on Saturday.” Brighton took the game to City and struck first through Malick Yalcouye. Mateo Kovačić levelled, but the visitors regained the advantage through Georginio Rutter, who also had a shot tipped onto the bar by Geronimo Rulli and hit the side-netting after rounding the keeper. City’s route back into the game came after the introduction of Jeremy Doku, whose arrival lifted the crowd. Vitor Reis deflected in a Rayan Cherki free-kick to take the game to penalties. Kovačić missed from the spot but Rulli saved from Yasin Ayari and Lewis Dunk to send City through 4-3. It was an impressive performance from Rulli in place of first-choice Gianluigi Donnarumma, who was one of five players given a brief holiday by Maresca this week. But, despite concerns over Donnarumma’s form, Maresca made clear there was no suggestion of the Italian losing his place. “No, absolutely not from my point of view,” said Maresca when asked if Rulli could take over as number one. “He’s working well but he knows exactly his role, and there’s not any doubt about it.” City’s season continues under the shadow of last month’s guilty verdict on financial charges but Maresca has remained focused on on-field matters. His side are top of the Premier League and now have a League Cup quarter-final against third-tier Bradford to prepare for. He said: “It’s a different competition but the ambition has to be the same. “This is a new project with new players, a new manager. It started three months ago. “We need to do our business. That is winning games and, at the moment, we are doing that.”

item.title: CBS Sports' Jon Rothstein predicts breakout year for Iowa basketball guard
item.description: As Iowa men's basketball prepares to begin its 2026-27 campaign, CBS Sports college basketball analyst Jon Rothstein named Hawkeyes second-year guard Tate Sage as one of his 10 under-the-radar breakout players nationwide this season. There were moments of promise throughout last season for Sage, but this hard playing wing truly stood out for the Hawkeyes in the NCAA Tournament. The 6-foot-7 Sage tallied 19 points and eight rebounds in Iowa's Sweet 16 win over Nebraska and followed that effort up by posting 10 points and three rebounds against Illinois in the Elite Eight. Those two games were a glimpse of what's to come in 2026-27. Sage is a gamer. - Jon Rothstein, CBS Sports Sage showed flashes of promise last season, averaging 6.1 points and 2.1 rebounds per game on 49.3% shooting, 38.9% from the 3-point line, and 71.1% from the free-throw line in 37 games. Although Sage was an ancillary scoring option for the Hawkeyes last season, Rothstein views Sage as one of the Hawkeyes' rising offensive weapons this year as Ben McCollum enters Year 2 at the helm. Fans will be able to see Sage back in action during Iowa's season-opener against Lipscomb on Nov. 3 at Carver-Hawkeye Arena, which is scheduled to tip off at 7 p.m. CT and streaming on B1G+ . item.title: Can Josh Jacobs still be suspended? What to know after Packers RB's return
item.description: The Green Bay Packers got back one of their key offensive playmakers in Week 7. But questions remain about his future availability. Running back Josh Jacobs made his 2026 debut against the Detroit Lions on Oct. 25 after spending the first six weeks on the commissioner's exempt list . Jacobs, who faced two misdemeanor charges stemming from a domestic dispute with his ex-girlfriend in May, is still the subject of an ongoing NFL investigation. Here's everything to know about Jacobs' situation, from a timeline of events so far to what further discipline the veteran running back could face, if any: JOSH JACOBS: Packers RB breaks silence on arrest, Week 7 return: 'Still trying to learn' Josh Jacobs court case timeline May 23, 2026: Hobart-Lawrence Police Department responds to a domestic disturbance complaint involving Jacobs in the morning. May 26: Police arrest Jacobs for his involvement in the domestic dispute with his now ex-girlfriend. Jacobs faced five counts after his initial arrest: battery (domestic abuse), criminal damage to property (domestic abuse), disorderly conduct (domestic abuse), strangulation and suffocation, and intimidation of a victim. Aug. 27: Brown County District Attorney David L. Lasee submits a formal complaint to charge Jacobs with two misdemeanors: battery and criminal damage to property. Aug. 30: NFL places Jacobs on the commissioner's exempt list, a form of paid administrative leave, while the league performed an investigation into the running back's actions. Players on the list are not allowed to practice or attend games, and time on the exempt list can count toward a suspension retroactively if the league hands down such a punishment after its investigation. For the second charge – criminal damage to property – Jacobs reached a deferred judgment agreement. He will have to meet a list of conditions for the next 12 months in order to have that charge dismissed by the state: no further criminal acts, no contact with the victim, supervision, counseling and restitution payment to the victim. item.title: Harrogate 'embarrassed' by nine-man Carlisle
item.description: Harrogate Town boss Simon Weaver has been in charge of the club since 2008 and became co-owner earlier this month [Getty Images] Carlisle United's task against second-placed Harrogate Town in the National League on Wednesday looked difficult at kick-off. The Blues took an early lead against the visitors, who were on a five-game winning run, but then had former Arsenal man Miguel Azeez sent off after just 14 minutes. Their mission then went from hard to surely impossible when they were then reduced to nine men after only 30 minutes when fellow midfielder Harvey Bunker was also shown a straight red card. Two men light and with sixty minutes to play against a side who had started the game 10 places and 11 points better off? You could have forgiven home fans for fearing the worst. Instead, remarkably, Rob Elliot's men added to their lead immediately after half-time and ultimately wrapped up a stunning 3-0 win that will be talked about by the fans at Brunton Park for years to come. "I don't think they appreciate what they've just done," Elliot told BBC Radio Cumbria. "There was no luck tonight. It was just superb performances and I'm immensely proud. "I'm hoping it's a catalyst for us to unite and make sure we carry on that momentum. If we can produce this every week then we become a monster and be unstoppable. "Tonight epitomised what I want from the staff, the players and the club. "When you are reduced to playing for pure passion, heart, desire and energy it becomes evident of what it means." The former Newcastle goalkeeper said it was "the most incredible" game of his playing or managerial career and said the players would be given an impromptu but hard-earned day off on Thursday before they play at Altrincham on Saturday. 'We didn't handle the situation' Emotions in the other dressing room could hardly have been more contrasting. Harrogate boss and co-owner Simon Weaver accused his side of "believing the hype" that their winning run had produced. When asked to sum up his emotions he told BBC Radio York: "Embarrassed to be honest. "We came into it with brilliant form but it looked like as a team and a collective we believed the hype coming into the game. "However, going down to 10 men and then nine men the emphasis was on us to show the required quality on the ball that we have done all season up to this point and we're certainly disappointed and fell well below the standards set so far this season. "We looked well off it. We didn't handle the situation. Full credit to Carlisle, they deserved to win but we have to look at our performance." The Sulphurites, who travel to Forest Green on Saturday, are now 10 points off runaway leaders Boreham Wood.

item.title: Jamie Carragher wants Liverpool to bring back Trent Alexander-Arnold: ‘He made a big mistake leaving’
item.description: Jamie Carragher wants Liverpool to bring back Trent Alexander-Arnold: ‘He made a big mistake leaving’ Jamie Carragher believes Liverpool should consider bringing Trent Alexander-Arnold back to Anfield, arguing that the England international made a major mistake by joining Real Madrid in 2025. The right-back has struggled to establish himself in Spain and has fallen to third in Jose Mourinho’s pecking order, behind Federico Valverde and Denzel Dumfries, prompting the former Liverpool defender to question his decision to leave his boyhood club. Carragher believes Alexander-Arnold made a mistake leaving Liverpool Trent’s move to Real Madrid was expected to mark the beginning of an exciting new chapter in his career after a long and successful spell at Liverpool. However, his time at the Santiago Bernabeu has fallen short of expectations, with limited playing time undermining his hopes of becoming a key figure in the Spanish capital. The numbers reflect his difficulties. Trent has made just four starts this season, while his involvement in Real Madrid’s recent 2-1 Clasico victory over Barcelona was restricted to a stoppage-time appearance. Losing prominence in the team. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) His reduced role has attracted the attention of Carragher, who believes Liverpool could benefit from reversing the transfer. Speaking on The Overlap podcast, the former Reds defender argued that Alexander-Arnold’s departure was a mistake, particularly given Liverpool’s ongoing difficulties at right-back and their struggle to replace his creative influence. “I would bring him back. I think he made a big mistake leaving. They are playing a midfielder at right-back, so even in El Clasico , Denzel Dumfries, the first-choice right-back, comes on as a substitute,” Carragher said, as quoted by SPORT . “So when you are the third option at a club, they clearly want you to look for a way out,” he added. Carragher believes Liverpool still miss Trent’s creativity Carragher’s argument extends beyond Trent’s individual circumstances. He believes Liverpool have yet to adequately replace the qualities the Englishman brought to their build-up play, particularly his passing range and ability to create chances. Behind Valverde and Dumfries in the pecking order at Real Madrid. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) “Ronnie (Ronald Araujo) has been fantastic, but we have a problem with the build-up play from our full-backs. We have certainly missed his creativity,” he explained. Carragher nevertheless acknowledged that any potential reunion would need to make sense from a footballing perspective. Wanting Trent back does not automatically mean a transfer would be straightforward, particularly given the circumstances of his departure and his current contract situation at Real Madrid. Moreover, the England international himself is not thinking about a potential departure and remains determined to turn things around and reclaim his place in Mourinho’s plans.

item.title: Canelo vs Mbilli: Start time, undercard and how to watch fight this weekend
item.description: Canelo Alvarez will return to the ring this weekend, challenging Christian Mbilli for the WBC super-middleweight title in Riyadh . Although the Saudi city has been the target of deadly attacks in recent weeks , Canelo has arrived ahead of his first fight in 13 months , after he was outpointed by fellow great Terence Crawford in Las Vegas. Against Mbilli, the 36-year-old Canelo faces a stern task; the Cameroonian is the younger man, at 31, and he enters his first title defence with an unbeaten record. Canelo Alvarez (right) at the weigh-in for his fight with Terence Crawford (Getty) Last time out, on the Canelo vs Crawford undercard, Mbilli fought Lester Martinez to a brutal draw to retain the interim WBC title, but he was later upgraded to regular champion when Crawford retired. Can Canelo prove that he is still among the best in the world? Or, as he returns from elbow surgery, will he show himself to be in the twilight of his great career? Here’s all you need to know. When is the fight? Canelo vs Mbilli will take place on Saturday 31 October at the ANB Arena in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The main card is expected to begin at 4pm GMT (9am PT / 11am CT / 12pm ET), with main-event ring walks following at 8.30pm GMT (1.30pm PT / 3.30pm CT / 4.30pm ET). How can I watch it? The event will stream live exclusively on DAZN pay-per-view at a cost of £24.99 ($79.99 in the US), and on DAZN Ultimate Tier – which is priced at £24.99 per month. You can purchase the fight or an Ultimate Tier subscription here. Will the event go ahead, and why is this a question? The organisation of the fight card has been the subject of intense speculation in recent weeks, due to numerous deadly attacks on Riyadh’s airports. Per Saudi authorities, more than 300 people have been left injured and at least 21 dead, due to strikes by the Yemen-aligned Houthis. The international airport has reopened, but the US Department of State has urged citizens to “reconsider travel to Saudi Arabia due to risk of drone and missile targeting", while areas near the Yemen border have been listed as such: “do not travel due to terrorism”. item.title: Barcelona president wants to sign Premier League star to reinforce the defence
item.description: Barcelona president wants to sign Premier League star to reinforce the defence Barcelona are staring at an important January transfer window ahead, where the club must secure reinforcements in the defensive unit. The recent injuries to Jules Kounde, Eric Garcia, Xavi Espart and Andreas Christensen have laid bare the club’s lack of depth in the area. As such, Barcelona are expected to enter the market for a new defender. The club have already been linked with a move for Stuttgart centre-back Finn Jeltsch , while signing a new fullback cannot be ruled out either. Laporta wants to sign Pedro Porro As reported by SPORT , Barcelona president Joan Laporta already has a desired reinforcement in mind, in the form of Pedro Porro. Porro has been a consistent performer for Spurs. (Photo by Ryan Pierse/Getty Images) The club have been monitoring the development of the Spanish international for quite some time and were linked with a move for the right-back during the backend of the summer transfer window. But the move did not materialise due to Tottenham’s astounding €60 million price tag. The defender also has a long-term contract in North London that doesn’t expire until 2031. Despite that, Porro remains open to the idea of returning to La Liga, which has kept his future open should any club are willing to meet Tottenham’s price tag. How does Porro fit into Barcelona? The potential addition of Pedro Porro can add some much-needed depth in the Barcelona backline, especially the fullback department. Porro is regarded highly by Joan Laporta. (Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images) The Spanish international offers a nice blend of balance when it comes to attack and defence in the right-flank and could be a potential upgrade over someone like Garcia, thus allowing Hansi Flick to operate the former Man City star in other positions. Porro also offers immense experience, having already played in La Liga while featuring in over 150 competitive matches for Tottenham. He has also won 24 caps for the Spanish national team and was a part of their World Cup winning squad in the summer. Porro’s expertise, therefore, could certain aid the Barcelona defence. However, the Spaniard could prove to be too costly for the Blaugrana , who may have an opportunity to sign Dodo on a free transfer next summer.

item.title: Miami Heat HC Erik Spoelstra highlights ‘monster’ Giannis Antetokounmpo’s impact in first win
item.description: Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images Giannis Antetokounmpo got his first win as a member of the Miami Heat on Wednesday, and his head coach has praised how he helped make it happen. The Miami Heat had a horrible start to the 2026-27 campaign, going 0-4 despite their new-look roster. Giannis Antetokounmpo’s move to South Beach looked like it was in big trouble, but they have now somewhat corrected course by getting their first win of the season. The Heat beat the Atlanta Hawks 129-117 in a hotly contested clash, taking a lead in the first quarter and seeing it through to the end. Bam Adebayo and Giannis combined for 48 points, while Andrew Wiggins, Pelle Larson, and Tim Hardaway Jr. also made some big contributions. After the game, Erik Spoelstra had some praise for his new superstar. Erik Spoelstra claims Giannis Antetokounmpo played a ‘smart game’ against Atlanta Giannis had 24 points, to go along with a whopping 18 rebounds and three assists. He claimed a steal and a block as well, getting his points quite efficiently during the game. The Greek Freak took only two more shots than Bam, and only six more than two of the closest role-players. Talking to the press having secured their win, Coach Spo had some kind words for the 31-year-old and the role he played against the Hawks. “Giannis will have bigger nights than this offensively. But I thought he really played a smart game,” Spoelstra said. Allowing the other guys to really have an impact and he asserted himself when he felt like he needed to. He was a monster on the glass. On both ends. It just seemed like whenever there needed to be a momentum play, he had his fingerprints on it at key points in the game.” This is high praise for Antetokounmpo from his coach. While he can certainly score more points than this, he ideally shouldn’t have to. If Miami can continue playing cohesively with Adebayo also putting up strong numbers, then the sky is the limit for what they can achieve. item.title: Rybakina secures year-end number one ranking
item.description: Rybakina has won three Grand Slams in her career [Getty Images] Elena Rybakina secured the year-end women's singles number one ranking by beating Yulia Putintseva in the last 16 of the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo. The 6-2 6-3 victory for Rybakina means she cannot be overtaken in the closing weeks of a stellar year in which she has won the Australian Open and US Open titles. She will play former US Open runner-up Leylah Fernandez, who she beat 6-2 6-2 in the Ningbo Open final, in the quarter-finals. The 27-year-old Rybakina, who represents Kazakhstan, beat Sabalenka in the finals of the Slams in Melbourne and New York this year and also usurped the Belarusian to become world number one on the way to her US Open victory in September. A quarter-final victory over China's Zheng Qinwen at the US Open made sure she would move to the top of the singles rankings for the first time. Rybakina triumphed at the Ningbo Open last week to win her fourth title of 2026 and, after a first-round bye in Tokyo, served six aces and produced 25 winners in beating Putintseva, who also competes for Kazakhstan. Rybakina's next tournament will be the defence of her singles title at the season-ending WTA Finals, which take place from 8-15 November in Indian Wells. 'Just a number' - Rybakina's rise to world number one Rybakina's journey to world number one Rybakina's push for the world number one ranking started at the end of 2025. After losing to Sabalenka in the quarter-finals of the Wuhan Open last October, Rybakina took the Ningbo Open title one week later before beating Sabalenka to win the season-ending WTA Finals. She carried that momentum into 2026, getting the better of Sabalenka again but this time in a major final. She beat her fellow big server in three competitive sets to win the Australian Open - her second Slam title almost four years after her first at Wimbledon. Since then, Sabalenka has come out on top in their Indian Wells final and Miami Open semi-final, but Rybakina took the Stuttgart title on clay as Sabalenka's form fluctuated. After disappointing early exits at the French Open and Wimbledon, Rybakina reached the final in Toronto, losing in straight sets to Iga Swiatek. Rybakina's quest to overtake long-time rankings leader Sabalenka suffered another setback when she was forced to retire injured from her Cincinnati Open quarter-final against Swiatek. Rybakina later revealed that the left ankle problem, which hindered her movement and prevented her pushing off properly when serving, had been "bothering me for a long period of time" but was something she felt she had "under control". Speaking before the US Open, Rybakina admitted her preparation "wasn't great" as she was unable to train for much of the week leading into the tournament. item.title: Hampton Morris takes bronze at weightlifting worlds after dramatic final lift, jury decision
item.description: For about 90 seconds, American weightlifter Hampton Morris was listed as a world champion. On the final lift at worlds in China, Morris appeared to successfully clean-and-jerk 189 kilograms (416 pounds). Multiple referees ruled it a good lift, but four jury members disagreed in real time due to elbow movement, according to broadcast commentary. While commentators said he was listed in first place on the arena scoreboard, the jury deliberated with video replay for more than a minute, deciding whether it was a clean lift. Video is here . It ruled no lift due to "bending and extending," according to the International Weightlifting Federation (IWF) . So Morris went from winning by one kilogram — and becoming the first U.S. man to win a senior world title since 1969 — to earning his second consecutive bronze medal in the 65kg division. “I’m entirely proud of what I did," Morris said, according to the IWF. "I showed exactly what I’m capable of, and I know I’ll be capable of more next time. “This was not the result I wanted or have worked for, but it’s about as close as I could have gotten. I’m showing the work I’m putting in, and I’m excited for my future.” Morris, from Marietta, Georgia, won bronze in the 61kg division at the 2024 Paris Games, becoming the first U.S. man to make an Olympic weightlifting podium since 1984. At 20, he was the youngest U.S. men's weightlifting medalist since 1956, according to Olympedia.org. item.description: Liam Scales rues dropping two points, but praises teammate Jota Liam Scales last night gave his thoughts in the wake of yet another below par performance from Celtic, in the 2-2 draw against Dundee United at Celtic Park… Liam Scales of Celtic scores Celtic v Dundee United, Scottish Premiership, Celtic Park, 28 October 2026. Photo Mark Runnacles IMAGO Shutterstock Speaking of his anguish at dropping two points at home to Jim Goodwin’s well drilled side, the Celtic defender acknowledged the ‘sloppy’ first half period where two soft goals were both conceded inside a few minutes. Celtic v Dundee United, Scottish Premiership, Celtic Park, 28 October 2026. item.title: Chris Finch and Steve Kerr Call Out the NBA’s Flopping Crackdown
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Chris Finch wanted the NBA to clean up flopping. He just thinks the league is targeting the wrong players. Steve Kerr’s preferred approach comes with a different name for the league: the “No Bulls*** Association.” Before Wednesday’s Warriors–Timberwolves game, both coaches questioned how the NBA is enforcing its crackdown. Their comments followed three consecutive flopping calls late in Tuesday’s Portland-Los Angeles game. The refs called THREE flopping technicals in 2 minutes 😭 pic.twitter.com/eAeeSN9Prz — BrickCenter (@BrickCenter_) October 28, 2026 Finch wants more attention on offensive players manufacturing free throws. Kerr wants officials empowered to reject the tricks players use to manipulate calls. Both support removing flopping. Their frustration is that the enforcement keeps missing what bothers them most. Chris Finch thinks the NBA has its priorities wrong Credit: Nick Wosika-USA TODAY Sports Finch’s complaint was specific: punishing defensive embellishment does little to address offensive foul-baiting. “I think where they got it wrong is all these flops they’re calling on the defense, and that’s not what the people want out of the game,” Finch said . “They want the flops on the offensive players out of the game.” He questioned whether the league’s interpretation matches the behavior fans recognize as flopping. His principal concern is players falling down to turn ordinary possessions into trips to the foul line. “What they care about is that the offensive players are baiting the game and falling down and getting unnecessary free throws,” Finch continued. “That’s what they care about because that’s not really in the spirit of why everyone wants to tune in and watch.” That is different from arguing that officials should simply call fewer fouls. Finch wants the NBA to distinguish legitimate attempts to score from actions designed primarily to provoke a whistle. A defender exaggerating contact can deserve scrutiny. But if offensive players continue benefiting from their own performances, the crackdown leaves a substantial part of the problem intact. Finch believes those offensive actions deserve greater emphasis. item.description: The NFL trade deadline , which expires at 4 p.m. ET on Nov. 10, is already coming into sharper focus now that the Indianapolis Colts have started unloading their most prized players in order to begin setting the table for a long-overdue rebuild as well as enticing whomever their next general manager will be now that Chris Ballard is no longer in the picture . Interim Indy GM Ed Dodds got busy getting his hands dirty on Tuesday, Oct. 27, when he traded perennial All-Pro G Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and, later in the day, sent three-time Pro Bowl DT DeForest Buckner back to his original team, the San Francisco 49ers . Those moves are probably indicative of others we’re likely to see leading up to the cutoff date – teams exporting players on expiring contracts, as Nelson and Buckner are, that will generally have minimal ramifications on their salary caps yet will likely also temper compensation. For instance, numerous Colts fans on social media clearly didn’t believe the team got sufficient value for Nelson, though a third- and fifth-round pick are probably a decent return given Seattle is only guaranteed a 10-game rental while hoping to get bonus time from him in the playoffs. When the Baltimore Ravens surrendered a second-round pick as part of their deal for former Philadelphia Eagles O-lineman Cam Jurgens earlier this month, they were also getting a player who’s under contract through the 2029 season. Moving forward, talents like Los Angeles Chargers OLB Khalil Mack , Tampa Bay Buccaneers OLB YaYa Diaby, Tennessee Titans RB Tony Pollard and perhaps even Las Vegas Raiders QB Kirk Cousins are in similar circumstances – gentlemen set to hit free agency in 2027 but who could get moved sooner if their current teams believe they can do better by obtaining capital going into next year’s touted draft as opposed to whatever compensatory selections they’d otherwise realize in 2028. item.title: How Many Aces Can Two Players Hit in Just Two Sets?
item.description: Sep 5, 2012; Queens, NY, USA; Andy Roddick (USA) waves to the crowd after his match against Juan Martin Del Potro (ARG) on day ten of the 2012 US Open at Billie Jean King National Tennis Center. Del Potro won 6-7, 7-6, 6-2, 6-4. Mandatory Credit: Susa… | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Yesh Ginsburg Yours truly was watching Tallon Griekspoor take on Max Schoenhaus at the European Open in Brussels, enjoying what was otherwise a fairly typical afternoon of indoor tennis, when it occurred to me that there had been an unusually large number of aces, which naturally led to the rather pointless but suddenly irresistible question of just how many aces two professional tennis players could hit in a match that lasted only two sets, and whether the two gentlemen were anywhere near the record. By that stage, they had already combined for more than 25. And by the time Schoenhaus won the second set, the count, according to the live statistics I was following, had reached 39. Griekspoor had hit 28. Schenhaus had contributed another 11. Had the Dutchman managed to finish the match in straight sets, that would have been an extraordinary number, so, naturally, I went looking for the record. And discovered that some tennis players have apparently spent entire afternoons doing little more than serving balls past one another. Five Extraordinary Two-Set Ace Festivals Reilly Opelka vs John Isner — 60 aces (Dallas 2022) This is the gold standard , and it is hard to imagine a more appropriate pairing. Opelka defeated Isner 7-6 7-6 in the Dallas Open semi-finals, with the two Americans combining for an astonishing 60 aces. Opelka hit 39 while Isner managed a comparatively modest 21. Neither player faced a single break point, but the most extraordinary part was the second-set tiebreak, which Opelka eventually won 24-22. That is 46 points played just to determine one tiebreak. Opelka saved ten set points and needed eight match points to finally end the contest. His 39 aces also established the ATP Tour record for the most aces by one player in a two-set match, based on records dating back to 1991. item.description: Motorsport photo The MotoGP Sports Entertainment Group (MGPSEG), the championship's commercial rights holder, remains fully committed to staging the Qatar Grand Prix, scheduled for next weekend after being postponed by almost six months from its original date. The conflict that broke out in February between the US-Israeli alliance and Iran has created a climate of instability across the Gulf region which, although less severe than during the opening months of the war, remains unresolved. For several weeks, most MotoGP riders have expressed reservations about the prospect of travelling to a region where tensions remain high and hostilities could flare up again at any moment. More than three-quarters of the grid have voiced their opposition to the trip, in contrast to MGPSEG's position that the guarantees provided by the Qatari government are sufficient. Following Wednesday's meeting at the Sepang circuit offices in Malaysia, attended by the riders and most of the teams' managers, it was Carmelo Ezpeleta, the promoter's CEO, who sat down with them on Thursday. Motorsport.com understands that the executive reiterated his position to those present, who left the meeting with the impression that the event would go ahead regardless of whether individual riders decided not to attend. Ezpeleta reminded the riders that their contracts bind them to their respective teams, which would ultimately be responsible for any penalties arising from a failure to fulfil their obligations. MotoGP riders stand for the playing of the National Anthems MotoGP riders stand for the playing of the National Anthems Last week in Australia, the riders asked MGPSEG to provide a series of written guarantees concerning their safety and the protection that would be afforded to the paddock in Qatar should the crisis escalate while personnel were in the country. The promoter insists that such guarantees fall outside its remit and are the responsibility of the Qatari government. Motorsport.com understands that Qatar has submitted a document committing to respond in the event of an emergency, although the riders are seeking more specific assurances. In this regard, Carlos Ezpeleta, MGPSEG's deputy CEO, is expected to arrive in Malaysia in the coming hours, and it will be his responsibility to outline the guarantees being offered by the country. Within the teams, most personnel are reluctant to travel to Qatar, although attitudes vary considerably from one individual to another. Yamaha, for example, intends to send the smallest possible number of staff, with Honda planning a similar approach. Meanwhile, several television broadcasters holding the championship's broadcasting rights have already indicated that they do not intend to send any personnel to Lusail. item.title: The Billion-Dollar Reason MLB Team Owners Are Willing To Risk A Lockout
item.description: As the Milwaukee Brewers celebrated their first-ever World Series championship on the Tampa Bay Rays’ home turf at Tropicana Field on Wednesday night, the sense of finality that always accompanies the final out of the postseason felt more intense than usual. With Major League Baseball’s collective bargaining agreement with its players’ union set to expire on December 1, most league insiders expect this off-season to extend well beyond pitchers and catchers’ typical reporting date for spring training in mid-February. In fact, as players and team owners dig in their heels for their most contentious battle since the strike that canceled the 1994 World Series, a labor stoppage is seen as all but guaranteed—the only question is whether it will wipe out some or all of the 2027 season. Team owners are insistent on implementing a salary cap, similar to the systems in the NBA, the NFL and the NHL that restrict club payrolls and in some cases individual players’ compensation—a concept that the MLB union has long viewed as a deal-breaker. Owners have not seriously put the issue on the table since the 1994-95 strike, when they attempted to impose a salary cap unilaterally and begin the 1995 season with replacement players in an effort that was stymied by the National Labor Relations Board and then-federal district judge Sonia Sotomayor. Now, owners and commissioner Rob Manfred say a cap is needed to level the playing field between big-market, free-spending clubs like the Los Angeles Dodgers and smaller-market rivals shelling out less than a quarter as much for their rosters. But there is another financial motivation behind MLB’s renewed push: Investment bankers believe that a salary cap, combined with more equitable revenue-sharing rules, would significantly boost team values for a league that has largely been left behind by its peers in basketball and football. Forbes And with much more money at stake than in the labor battle three decades ago, owners aren’t expected to back down easily. “If you lose a season and the CBA is positive for the owners, I think asset values will continue to go up,” says Sal Galatioto, president of Galatioto Sports Partners. “If you lose a season and you come out with basically the same economic system you have now, then the owners are going to take a big hit. I don’t think it’s the length of the lockout that matters as much as the result of the lockout.” MLB franchise values have already been on a steady climb, with the average reaching an estimated $2.9 billion by March—up 126% from 2016’s $1.3 billion and rising by a factor of nearly 15 since Forbes began valuing sports teams in 1998. item.title: Joe Burrow comments on Bengals trade deadline speculation
item.description: The Cincinnati Bengals are sitting at 4-2 to start the season after an electric win over the Baltimore Ravens this past weekend, 35-13. Despite the good start to the 2026 season, the Bengals still have plenty of needs to help solidify the roster before the trade deadline. The Bengals could still use another corner, safety, linebacker, running back, and now tight end with season-ending injuries to Erick All Jr. and Tanner Hudson. Fans have seen the Bengals in rumors for guys like Zach Baun and Johnathan Taylor, but there have been zero legitimate reports suggesting this will actually happen so far. Joe Burrow was asked about the trade deadline rumors during his weekly press conference with local media, and he shared his thoughts regarding them. “Number one, I feel really good about our team and the guys we have in there,” Burrow said. “Number two, I think every GM in football is probably exploring all options at this point, and very few ever end up materializing. But that’s something that I think all those guys think about critically, and whether it ends up happening or not, who knows. “But I feel really good about the team we have in there.” Burrow was then asked about the rarity of the Bengals front office making trades, and of course, Dexter Lawrence was brought up. “I don’t think there’s very often that a player like Dex becomes available. And then for one first-round pick in a high-need position for us…I think all those things together kind of created the perfect storm of a situation for us to involve ourselves. “And yeah, obviously it’s worked out great for us, and we couldn’t be happier with it,” Burrow stated. It will be fun to see what shakes out before the deadline, but it is clear the team is confident in the guys they have in the building right now.

item.description: Manchester City Monitoring Ajax Teenage Sensation Amid Stiff European Competition Hugo Viana and co are plotting a move for Ajax starlet Abdellah Ouazane. More Videos The Eredivisie has long served as one of European football's most prolific breeding grounds for elite young talent. Whether they come in the form of midfield orchestrators like Frenkie de Jong or tricky forwards such as Cody Gakpo, Dutch clubs are synonymous with technically adept youngsters honing their craft before a big-money move to title contenders on foreign soil. All that means that eyebrows are naturally raised any time top European sides begin monitoring the latest breakout talent in the Netherlands. If reports are to be believed, this one could be bound for Manchester - although Enzo Maresca's side could face stiff competition for his signature from other footballing giants. As reported by Tutto Atalanta and relayed by Sport Witness , Manchester City have entered the race for Ajax teenager Abdellah Ouazane. Having progressed through the academy ranks in Amsterdam since the age of seven, the 17-year-old midfielder has transitioned into a regular player for the senior side this season, making 10 appearances in the Eredivisie alongside two outings in the UEFA Conference League group stage. His growing presence in senior football was underlined during a standout substitute performance in a 2-0 win over Atalanta, where he netted his first European goal off the bench having already scored twice domestically. Before establishing himself in the first team at Ajax, the Moroccan youth international did something few players can stake a claim to: turning down a move to Real Madrid. Despite a deal with the Spanish giants being practically finalised, the youngster opted to remain in the Netherlands to ensure regular minutes for his development. It is safe to say that decision is now yielding tangible rewards on the pitch. With Ouazane’s contract only running until 2028, interested clubs are expecting Ajax to face mounting pressure to sell if they want to come away with the best possible fee. The report identifies both Manchester City and Juventus as clubs monitoring the situation closely. While the Italian side can point to their successful Next Gen development pathway, Manchester City also have an established track record of nurturing young prospects, many of whom are currently seeing regular minutes at elite clubs both inside and outside of the Premier League. While Ouazane focuses on continuing to secure regular minutes in Amsterdam, this is a player City fans may want to keep an eye on in case reported interest develops further.

item.description: Photo by Ian Maddox for The Washington Post via Getty Images The Dallas Mavericks have had an interesting start to the new NBA season, winning three of their first five games. The latest of those wins came against the Oklahoma City Thunder on Wednesday night – a dominant 120-96 victory at the American Airlines Centre. Skip Bayless seems to be impressed by the Mavs, but he can’t help but wonder how much better they would’ve been had they not traded Anthony Davis earlier this year. Skip Bayless says Dallas Mavericks would be contenders if they had kept Anthony Davis The Dallas Mavericks traded Davis to the Washington Wizards in an eight-player deal. The 33-year-old was joined by D’Angelo Russell, Jaden Hardy and Dante Exum on his way to the capital, while Chris Middleton, Marvin Bagley III, AJ Johnson and Malachi Branham moved in the opposite direction, along with two first-round and three second-round draft picks. One of the reasons for the trade was Davis’ injury struggles during his time at Dallas. He missed over 50 regular-season games. Those problems, combined with his age, made the decision-makers at the Mavs feel he had to be moved on, but Bayless appears to have suggested that they made a mistake. In a tweet after watching Dallas win on Wednesday night, he claimed that the Mavericks would be contenders had they kept hold of Davis and played him alongside Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving. He tweeted: “I still don’t understand why the Mavericks traded Anthony Davis. Cooper Flagg, Kyrie, AD… contender.” On his day, Davis is a sensational player, but his luck with injuries has made him unreliable for the Mavs to keep him long-term. He missed over 50 regular season games for them. The trade decision has also been justified, as Davis missed the final 45 games of last season due to a hand injury he suffered while still with the Mavericks. He only made his Wizards debut in this campaign’s opener despite joining them in February. Davis is great, but the Mavs were right to move him on.
